correctness.rationale: Graph geodesics in H(d,q) yield rectangular hull closure, established also in prior Cartesian-product convexity literature. For root x, each coordinate generates a nonempty matching-row set M_i; inclusion minimality is equivalent to each premise row occurring as some singleton M_i. This proves 2<=r<=d, yields r! division without row-duplication issues, and produces the inclusion-exclusion formula with per-coordinate total q^r-(q-1)^r and removed singleton weight (q-1)^(r-1). For r=d all coordinates are distinct singleton patterns giving (q-1)^[d(d-1)]. General Horn stem necessity establishes the unique inclusion-minimal direct unit basis. A constructive family of (2^r-1)^(d-r)/r! stems at r=floor(d/2) yields exp(Omega(d^2)), with trivial exp(O(d^2)) upper bound; pair interval rules yield <N^3/2 chained rules. The proof addresses all integers d,q>=2. Standalone verify.py independently enumerated seven small cases and compared interval/rectangle closure on 984 samples; these are finite corroborations only.

value.rationale: A single natural family of closure systems has a complete exact size distribution of all indispensable one-pass unit Horn premises, with a nonbinary alphabet parameter, an attained maximum stem rank, and a provable superpolynomial blowup in representation size relative to a polynomial-size chained geodesic interval basis. This establishes an operational expressivity/description-size boundary, not merely a small parameter table; the mathematically relevant distinction is simultaneous one-pass inference versus iteration. The binary rank counts are classical, but the weighted nonbinary and logical-representation synthesis motivates the precise invariant. Meaningfulness is qualified by the elementary weighted-cover reduction and possible implicit precedence.
